quiz_met6:1.q: After several days of starvation, a patient's cells increase breakdown of their own proteins to release amino acids. Which route does the lecture single out as particularly important in this state?
quiz_met6:1.r: The cellular proteins slide notes that KFERQ-dependent degradation in the auto-lysosome is particularly important under starvation conditions (p. 816); tissue proteins are otherwise spared if possible (p. 840).

quiz_met6:10.q: After a protein-rich meal, valine, leucine and isoleucine largely escape breakdown in the liver and are degraded in extrahepatic tissues. Absence of which hepatic enzyme explains this?
quiz_met6:10.r: Branched-chain aminotransferase, the first enzyme of the pathway, is marked 'Absent in liver', so these amino acids are not primarily degraded there (p. 826).

quiz_met6:11.q: A patient on a carbohydrate-free diet depends on amino acid carbon for gluconeogenesis. According to the lecture's classification, which amino acid cannot supply carbon for glucose?
quiz_met6:11.r: Lysine and leucine appear only in the ketogenic boxes (acetoacetyl-CoA or acetyl-CoA). Isoleucine, threonine, tryptophan and phenylalanine are listed as both glucogenic and ketogenic (p. 825).

quiz_met6:12.q: A newborn screening test identifies maple syrup urine disease. Which enzyme is deficient?
quiz_met6:12.r: Maple syrup urine disease is marked on the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex, the second step, which turns the alpha-keto acids into acyl-CoA derivatives (p. 826).

quiz_met6:13.q: Mitochondria in a respiring hepatocyte maintain a proton-motive force across the inner membrane. Compared with the intermembrane space, how does the lecture describe the matrix?
quiz_met6:13.r: Protons are pumped out of the matrix, so the matrix (N side) is alkaline ('inside alkaline', delta pH) and negative ('inside negative', delta psi) (p. 829).

quiz_met6:14.q: Isolated mitochondria are supplied with NADH as the only electron donor. By the lecture's counts for Complexes I, III and IV, how many protons are pumped per pair of electrons passed to oxygen?
quiz_met6:14.r: The overview labels 4 H+ at Complex I, 4 H+ at Complex III and 2 H+ at Complex IV, so 10 per NADH electron pair. Electrons entering at Complex II skip Complex I and give 6 (p. 829).

quiz_met6:15.q: A student ranks the electron acceptors of the respiratory chain by standard reduction potential. Which acceptor has the highest value?
quiz_met6:15.r: Oxygen to water has the highest standard reduction potential in her table (0.8166 V), above cytochrome a3 (0.35 V); electrons move to carriers of increasing reduction potential and end at O2 (p. 831).

quiz_met6:16.q: In a neuron, electrons from glycolytic NADH are carried into mitochondria by the glycerol 3-phosphate shuttle. At which carrier do they enter the respiratory chain?
quiz_met6:16.r: Mitochondrial glycerol 3-phosphate dehydrogenase passes the electrons through FAD to ubiquinone (QH2), which feeds Complex III. Skipping Complex I is why this shuttle is less efficient (p. 833, p. 834).

quiz_met6:17.q: A man swallows an unknown white powder and develops severe lactic acidosis with cherry-red skin, then improves after hydroxocobalamin. What did the toxin bind?
quiz_met6:17.r: Cyanide targets Complex IV (cytochrome oxidase) by binding ferric iron (Fe3+) and is treated with hydroxocobalamin (B12); CO binds ferrous iron (Fe2+) of hemoglobin and is treated with pure O2 (p. 836, p. 837).

quiz_met6:18.q: An antibiotic plugs the proton path of ATP synthase and stops its rotor. Through which subunits do protons normally cross the inner membrane?
quiz_met6:18.r: Protons cross through Fo: they enter at the a subunit, ride the c ring, and leave to the matrix side. Alpha and beta subunits of F1 make the ATP (p. 838).

quiz_met6:19.q: In an experiment, 24 protons flow through one ATP synthase. According to the lecture's numbers for a full rotor turn, how many ATP are produced?
quiz_met6:19.r: Her rotor slide gives 8 protons per 360 degree turn and 3 ATP per turn, so 24 protons is 3 turns and 9 ATP (p. 838).

quiz_met6:2.q: A sprinter's skeletal muscle is oxidizing amino acids for energy and must send the amino groups to the liver. Which carrier does the lecture assign to this tissue?
quiz_met6:2.r: Extracellular NH4+ transport is by glutamine in most tissues and by alanine in skeletal muscle (p. 817); glutamate is the intracellular collector, not the blood carrier.

quiz_met6:20.q: During myocardial ischemia, ATPase inhibitory factor 1, abbreviated IF1, keeps ATP synthase from running in reverse and using up ATP. How does it act?
o: IF1 locks Fo at acidic pH
IF1 locks F1 at acidic pH
IF1 locks F1 at alkaline pH
IF1 locks Fo at alkaline pH
IF1 frees F1 at acidic pH
quiz_met6:20.r: IF1 locks the F1 portion under hypoxic conditions so the enzyme does not run in reverse and use up ATP, and it is triggered by acidic pH of about 6.5 (p. 838).

quiz_met6:3.q: A patient with vitamin B6 deficiency cannot make enough pyridoxal 5'-phosphate. Which step of nitrogen handling is directly impaired?
quiz_met6:3.r: Aminotransferases move the amino group of any amino acid onto alpha-ketoglutarate to make glutamate, and they use pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), the active coenzyme form of vitamin B6 (p. 818).

quiz_met6:4.q: A toxin blocks export of one urea cycle intermediate from the mitochondrial matrix to the cytosol. Which intermediate is trapped where it was made?
quiz_met6:4.r: Ornithine transcarbamylase makes citrulline in the mitochondrial matrix, and citrulline then moves to the cytosol for the remaining steps; ornithine travels the other way, cytosol to matrix (p. 822).

quiz_met6:5.q: In a tracer study of hepatocytes, one nitrogen of urea is traced to carbamoyl phosphate. Which molecule directly supplies the other nitrogen during the cytosolic steps?
quiz_met6:5.r: Urea's first nitrogen is free NH4+ carried in carbamoyl phosphate; the second comes from aspartate, added by argininosuccinate synthetase in step 2b (p. 822). The aspartate skeleton leaves as fumarate.

quiz_met6:6.q: A newborn is found to have no argininosuccinase activity in the liver. Which two products are no longer formed at the blocked step?
quiz_met6:6.r: Argininosuccinase (step 3) splits argininosuccinate into arginine and fumarate; urea and ornithine come from arginase (step 4), and citrulline and phosphate from ornithine transcarbamylase (step 1) (p. 822).

quiz_met6:7.q: A hepatocyte's carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I shows low activity despite ample ammonium, bicarbonate and ATP. Which molecule is the direct activator that it lacks?
quiz_met6:7.r: N-acetylglutamate (NAG) activates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I. Arginine acts one step earlier: it activates N-acetylglutamate synthase, which makes NAG from acetyl-CoA and glutamate (p. 823).

quiz_met6:8.q: A patient adopts a high-protein diet for several months. According to the lecture, which molecule binds its nuclear receptor to increase transcription of urea cycle enzymes?
quiz_met6:8.r: Her slide says a high protein diet increases the frequency of glucagon release, leading to cortisol release; cortisol binds its nuclear receptor and activates transcription (p. 823). Glucagon is upstream, not the receptor ligand.

quiz_met6:9.q: A researcher follows labeled carbons from tyrosine into newly made glucose. Through which citric acid cycle intermediate do they enter?
quiz_met6:9.r: Phenylalanine and tyrosine are the two amino acids whose glucogenic carbons enter the citric acid cycle as fumarate; their ketogenic carbons go to acetoacetyl-CoA (p. 825).

quiz_met6_b:1.q: A toddler's intestine fails to absorb neutral amino acids such as tryptophan, while lysine and arginine are absorbed normally. Which disorder fits this pattern?
quiz_met6_b:1.r: The dietary protein slide lists two defects of intestinal amino acid absorption: Hartnup (neutral amino acids) and lysinuric protein intolerance (cationic amino acids) (p. 815).

quiz_met6_b:10.q: Electrons in the respiratory chain pass to carriers of increasing standard reduction potential. By the lecture's table of potentials, which direct transfer would be energetically unfavorable?
o: NADH to the FMN of Complex I
quiz_met6_b:10.r: The table rises from NADH (-0.320 V) through FMN, ubiquinone (0.045), cytochrome b, c1, c (0.254), a and a3 to oxygen (0.8166). Cytochrome c to ubiquinone runs from a higher to a lower potential, against the favorable direction (p. 831).

quiz_met6_b:11.q: A cardiac myocyte burning fatty acids feeds one acetyl-CoA into the citric acid cycle. By the lecture's ATP yield table, how many ATP does oxidizing that one acetyl-CoA produce?
quiz_met6_b:11.r: For the two acetyl-CoA from one glucose the table lists 6 NADH (15 ATP), 2 FADH2 (3 ATP) and 2 ATP or GTP (2), which is 20, so one acetyl-CoA gives 10 (p. 839).

quiz_met6_b:2.q: An extrahepatic cell that has run out of ATP can no longer load free ammonium onto its blood carrier. Which enzyme catalyzes this ATP-requiring step?
quiz_met6_b:2.r: In extra-hepatic tissues glutamine synthetase uses ATP to make gamma-glutamyl phosphate from glutamate, then adds ammonium to give glutamine; glutaminase is the liver mitochondrial enzyme that releases the ammonium again (p. 819).

quiz_met6_b:3.q: Hepatocytes are incubated with a carbon-labeled compound, and the label is recovered in the single carbon of urea. Which labeled molecule supplied that carbon?
quiz_met6_b:3.r: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I joins ammonium and bicarbonate using 2 ATP, and the bicarbonate carbon is the highlighted carbon that ends up in urea (p. 821, p. 822). Aspartate gives a nitrogen and leaves as fumarate.

quiz_met6_b:4.q: Arginine rises in a hepatocyte after a protein-rich meal, and carbamoyl phosphate synthesis speeds up within minutes. Which enzyme does arginine activate directly?
quiz_met6_b:4.r: N-acetylglutamate synthase is 'activated by Arginine'; it makes N-acetylglutamate from acetyl-CoA and glutamate, and N-acetylglutamate then activates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (p. 823).

quiz_met6_b:5.q: A strict vegan with cobalamin deficiency has low methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity. Entry of which amino acid's carbon skeleton into the citric acid cycle is directly impaired?
quiz_met6_b:5.r: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, cobalamin (B12) dependent, sits on the route into succinyl-CoA, which is the entry point for isoleucine, methionine, threonine and valine (p. 825). Leucine and lysine are ketogenic, and phenylalanine and tyrosine enter at fumarate.

quiz_met6_b:6.q: A labeled amino acid's carbon skeleton is recovered in both succinyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA, so it is both glucogenic and ketogenic. Which amino acid was labeled?
quiz_met6_b:6.r: Isoleucine is in the succinyl-CoA box (glucogenic) and the acetyl-CoA box (ketogenic). Valine and methionine reach only succinyl-CoA, leucine is ketogenic only, and tryptophan gives pyruvate, not succinyl-CoA (p. 825).

quiz_met6_b:7.q: Skeletal muscle transaminates more leucine than it needs for fuel. According to the lecture, in what form can the surplus carbon skeletons travel in blood to the liver?
quiz_met6_b:7.r: Branched-chain amino acids are not primarily degraded in liver, 'but alpha keto acids may be released into blood and transported to liver if they are not needed by the extra-hepatic tissue' (p. 826). The acyl-CoA derivatives come after the dehydrogenase step.

quiz_met6_b:8.q: In a cardiac myocyte, electrons from glycolytic NADH enter the matrix by the shuttle the lecture assigns to heart. Which molecule carries them across the inner membrane?
quiz_met6_b:8.r: Liver, kidney and heart use the malate-aspartate shuttle: NADH reduces oxaloacetate to malate, malate crosses on the malate-alpha-ketoglutarate transporter, and matrix malate dehydrogenase remakes NADH (p. 832). Glycerol 3-phosphate belongs to the skeletal muscle and brain shuttle (p. 833).

quiz_met6_b:9.q: Two victims of a house fire are poisoned, one by carbon monoxide and one by cyanide. According to the lecture, which statement applies only to the carbon monoxide victim?
quiz_met6_b:9.r: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin ferrous iron and prevents oxygen delivery to tissues, and is treated with pure oxygen. Failure of aerobic metabolism, lactic acidosis and bright red skin are listed as shared features, and hydroxocobalamin treats cyanide (p. 837).

Met 6: Urea Cycle and Electron Transport Chain (Jones) high-yield tables

Met 6: Urea Cycle and Electron Transport Chain (Jones). Your September first attempt on this lecture was 24/33. Page numbers are pages of the combined PDF, where the lecture runs pp. 808 to 840. Everything is from her slides unless labeled (outside the slides). The slides never spell out ATP, ADP, AMP, GTP, NAD, NADH, NADPH, FAD, FADH2, FMN, CoA, Pi, PPi, ETF, Fe-S, TCA or CO, so those expansions are standard names (outside the slides).
